sanskrit: ity uktāḥ sītayā ghoraṃ rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ kāś cij jagmus tad ākhyātuṃ rāvaṇasya tarasvinaḥ
english: Thus harshly addressed by Sītā, the rākṣasīs, overcome with rage, some of them went swiftly to report this to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ sītām upāgamya rākṣasyo ghoradarśanāḥ punaḥ paruṣam ekārtham anarthārtham athābruvan
english: Then those dreadful-looking rākṣasīs came back to Sītā and spoke harsh words again, all with one purpose — her ruin.

sanskrit: hantedānīṃ tavānārye sīte pāpaviniścaye rākṣasyo bhakṣayiṣyanti māṃsam etad yathāsukham
english: "Now, O ignoble Sītā, O one resolved upon sin, the rākṣasīs will eat this flesh of yours at their pleasure."

sanskrit: sītāṃ tābhir anāryābhir dṛṣṭvā saṃtarjitāṃ tadā rākṣasī trijaṭāvṛddhā śayānā vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing Sītā then being thus threatened by those ignoble ones, the aged rākṣasī Trijaṭā, lying there, spoke these words.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ khādatānāryā na sītāṃ bhakṣayiṣyatha janakasya sutām iṣṭāṃ snuṣāṃ daśarathasya ca
english: "Devour yourselves, O ignoble ones! You will not eat Sītā — she who is the beloved daughter of Janaka and the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: svapno hy adya mayā dṛṣṭo dāruṇo romaharṣaṇaḥ rākṣasānām abhāvāya bhartur asyā bhavāya ca
english: "For today I have seen a terrible dream that makes the hair stand on end — portending the destruction of the rākṣasas and the welfare of this one's husband."

sanskrit: evam uktās trijaṭayā rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ sarvā evābruvan bhītās trijaṭāṃ tām idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Trijaṭā, the rākṣasīs, overcome with anger and yet afraid, all said these words to her.

sanskrit: kathayasva tvayā dṛṣṭaḥ svapne 'yaṃ kīdṛśo niśi
english: "Tell us — what kind of dream did you see in the night?"

sanskrit: tāsāṃ śrutvā tu vacanaṃ rākṣasīnāṃ mukhodgatam uvāca vacanaṃ kāle trijaṭāsvapnasaṃśritam
english: Hearing the words that had issued from the mouths of the rākṣasīs, Trijaṭā spoke in due time these words concerning her dream.

sanskrit: gajadantamayīṃ divyāṃ śibikām antarikṣagām yuktāṃ vājisahasreṇa svayam āsthāya rāghavaḥ
english: "Rāghava himself mounted a divine celestial palanquin fashioned of elephant ivory, moving through the sky, yoked to a thousand horses —"

sanskrit: svapne cādya mayā dṛṣṭā sītā śuklāmbarāvṛtā sāgareṇa parikṣiptaṃ śvetaparvatam āsthitā rāmeṇa saṃgatā sītā bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā
english: "— and in the dream today I also saw Sītā clad in white garments, standing upon a white mountain encircled by the ocean, united with Rāma, like the radiance joined with the sun."

sanskrit: rāghavaś ca mayā dṛṣṭaś caturdantaṃ mahāgajam ārūḍhaḥ śailasaṃkāśaṃ cacāra sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "And I saw Rāghava mounted on a great four-tusked elephant, mountain-like, roaming together with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tatas tau naraśārdūlau dīpyamānau svatejasā śuklamālyāmbaradharau jānakīṃ paryupasthitau
english: "Then those two tiger-like men, blazing with their own splendor, clad in white garlands and garments, drew near to Jānakī."

sanskrit: tatas tasya nagasyāgre ākāśasthasya dantinaḥ bhartrā parigṛhītasya jānakī skandham āśritā
english: "Then, at the summit of that elephant standing in the sky, with her husband clasping her, Jānakī rested upon his shoulder."

sanskrit: bhartur aṅkāt samutpatya tataḥ kamalalocanā candrasūryau mayā dṛṣṭā pāṇibhyāṃ parimārjatī
english: "Then springing up from her husband's lap, the lotus-eyed one — so I saw — caressed the moon and sun with her two hands."

sanskrit: tatas tābhyāṃ kumārābhyām āsthitaḥ sa gajottamaḥ sītayā ca viśālākṣyā laṅkāyā upari sthitaḥ
english: "Then that best of elephants, mounted by those two princes and by the wide-eyed Sītā, stood above Laṅkā."

sanskrit: pāṇḍurarṣabhayuktena rathenāṣṭayujā svayam śuklamālyāmbaradharo lakṣmaṇena samāgataḥ lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā saha bhāryayā
english: "Himself clad in white garlands and garments, he came together with Lakṣmaṇa on a chariot drawn by eight white oxen, with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife Sītā."

sanskrit: vimānāt puṣpakād adya rāvaṇaḥ patito bhuvi kṛṣyapāṇaḥ striyā dṛṣṭo muṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇāmbaraḥ punaḥ
english: "Today Rāvaṇa was seen fallen from the Puṣpaka aerial chariot to the ground, dragged by the hands by a woman, shaven-headed and clad in black garments."

sanskrit: rathena kharayuktena raktamālyānulepanaḥ prayāto dakṣiṇām āśāṃ praviṣṭaḥ kardamaṃ hradam
english: "Adorned with red garlands and unguents, he departed on a chariot yoked with asses toward the southern quarter and entered a pool of mire."

sanskrit: kaṇṭhe baddhvā daśagrīvaṃ pramadā raktavāsinī kālī kardamaliptāṅgī diśaṃ yāmyāṃ prakarṣati
english: "A dark woman clad in red garments, her body smeared with mire, bound the ten-necked one by the neck and dragged him toward the southern quarter."

sanskrit: varāheṇa daśagrīvaḥ śiṃśumāreṇa cendrajit uṣṭreṇa kumbhakarṇaś ca prayāto dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: "Daśagrīva was carried off on a boar, Indrajit on a porpoise, and Kumbhakarṇa on a camel — all proceeding toward the southern quarter."

sanskrit: samājaś ca mahān vṛtto gītavāditraniḥsvanaḥ pibatāṃ raktamālyānāṃ rakṣasāṃ raktavāsasām
english: "A great assembly took place with the sounds of song and musical instruments, of rākṣasas wearing red garlands and red garments, drinking."

sanskrit: laṅkā ceyaṃ purī ramyā savājirathasaṃkulā sāgare patitā dṛṣṭā bhagnagopuratoraṇā
english: "And this lovely city of Laṅkā, filled with horses and chariots, was seen fallen into the ocean with its gateways and arches shattered."

sanskrit: pītva tailaṃ pranṛttāś ca prahasantyo mahāsvanāḥ laṅkāyāṃ bhasmarūkṣāyāṃ sarvā rākṣasayoṣitaḥ
english: "Having drunk oil and dancing about, laughing loudly, all the rākṣasa women were in Laṅkā made rough with ash."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇādayaś ceme sarve rākṣasapuṃgavāḥ raktaṃ nivasanaṃ gṛhya praviṣṭā gomayahrade
english: "And all these foremost rākṣasas, Kumbhakarṇa and the rest, clad in red garments, entered a pool of cow-dung."

sanskrit: apagacchata naśyadhvaṃ sītām āpnoti rāghavaḥ ghātayet paramāmarṣī sarvaiḥ sārdhaṃ hi rākṣasaiḥ
english: "Depart! Be gone! Rāghava will recover Sītā — he of supreme wrath will slay together with all the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: priyāṃ bahumatāṃ bhāryāṃ vanavāsam anuvratām bhartsitāṃ tarjitāṃ vāpi nānumaṃsyati rāghavaḥ
english: "Rāghava will not tolerate his beloved, his esteemed wife who followed him faithfully into forest exile, being threatened and terrified thus."

sanskrit: tad alaṃ krūravākyair vaḥ sāntvam evābhidhīyatām abhiyācāma vaidehīm etad dhi mama rocate
english: "Therefore enough of cruel words from you — let only gentle speech be spoken. Let us supplicate Vaidehī — this is what pleases me."

sanskrit: yasyā hy evaṃ vidhaḥ svapno duḥkhitāyāḥ pradṛśyate sā duḥkhair bahubhir muktā priyaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam
english: "For she who, afflicted with sorrow, beholds such a dream will be freed from many sorrows and attain her most beloved one."

sanskrit: bhartsitām api yācadhvaṃ rākṣasyaḥ kiṃ vivakṣayā rāghavād dhi bhayaṃ ghoraṃ rākṣasānām upasthitam
english: "Even though she has been threatened, seek her favor, O rākṣasīs — what good is further harshness? Terrible fear from Rāghava is now imminent for the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: praṇipāta prasannā hi maithilī janakātmajā alam eṣā paritrātuṃ rākṣasyo mahato bhayāt
english: "For Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, when pleased by obeisance, is capable of protecting the rākṣasīs from great danger."

sanskrit: api cāsyā viśālākṣyā na kiṃ cid upalakṣaye viruddham api cāṅgeṣu susūkṣmam api lakṣmaṇam
english: "And in the limbs of this wide-eyed one I perceive nothing contrary, not even the slightest inauspicious omen."

sanskrit: chāyā vaiguṇya mātraṃ tu śaṅke duḥkham upasthitam aduḥkhārhām imāṃ devīṃ vaihāyasam upasthitām
english: "Only the dimness of her luster gives me concern — that sorrow has come upon this goddess who does not deserve suffering, this one destined for the sky."

sanskrit: arthasiddhiṃ tu vaidehyāḥ paśyāmy aham upasthitām rākṣasendravināśaṃ ca vijayaṃ rāghavasya ca
english: "Indeed I see the attainment of Vaidehī's purpose now at hand — the destruction of the lord of rākṣasas and the victory of Rāghava."

sanskrit: nimittabhūtam etat tu śrotum asyā mahat priyam dṛśyate ca sphurac cakṣuḥ padmapatram ivāyatam
english: "And this is the omen for her to hear great good news — her eye is seen to quiver, lotus-petal-like and long."

sanskrit: īṣac ca hṛṣito vāsyā dakṣiṇāyā hy adakṣiṇaḥ akasmād eva vaidehyā bāhur ekaḥ prakampate
english: "And there is a slight bristling of the hair of her right side which is inauspicious, and suddenly one arm of Vaidehī trembles."

sanskrit: kareṇuhastapratimaḥ savyaś corur anuttamaḥ vepan sūcayatīvāsyā rāghavaṃ purataḥ sthitam
english: "And her left thigh, incomparable, resembling an elephant's trunk, quivering, seems to point out Rāghava standing before her."

sanskrit: pakṣī ca śākhā nilayaṃ praviṣṭaḥ punaḥ punaś cottamasāntvavādī sukhāgatāṃ vācam udīrayāṇaḥ punaḥ punaś codayatīva hṛṣṭaḥ
english: "And a bird that has entered its branch-nest, speaking excellent soothing words, joyfully seems to urge on again and again the utterance of welcoming words."

sanskrit: sā rākṣasendrasya vaco niśamya tad rāvaṇasyāpriyam apriyārtā sītā vitatrāsa yathā vanānte siṃhābhipannā gajarājakanyā
english: Hearing those words of Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas — words that were cruel and whose import was cruelty — Sītā, stricken with misery, trembled as a young elephant princess set upon by a lion at the forest's edge.

sanskrit: sā rākṣasī madhyagatā ca bhīrur vāgbhir bhṛśaṃ rāvaṇatarjitā ca kāntāramadhye vijane visṛṣṭā bāleva kanyā vilalāpa sītā
english: Surrounded by rākṣasīs and afraid, severely threatened with words by Rāvaṇa, left alone in the midst of a wilderness — Sītā lamented like a young girl abandoned in a deserted forest.

sanskrit: satyaṃ batedaṃ pravadanti loke nākālamṛtyur bhavatīti santaḥ yatrāham evaṃ paribhartsyamānā jīvāmi kiṃ cit kṣaṇam apy apuṇyā
english: "Truly do the wise say in this world that untimely death does not come — for here am I, wretched and without merit, living even a moment while being reviled thus."

sanskrit: sukhād vihīnaṃ bahuduḥkhapūrṇam idaṃ tu nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sthiraṃ me vidīryate yan na sahasradhādya vajrāhataṃ śṛṅgam ivācalasya
english: "Deprived of happiness and filled with much sorrow, my heart is surely firm — for it does not today split asunder in a thousand fragments like the peak of a mountain struck by the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: naivāsti nūnaṃ mama doṣam atra vadhyāham asyāpriyadarśanasya bhāvaṃ na cāsyāham anupradātum alaṃ dvijo mantram ivādvijāya
english: "Surely there is no fault in me that I should be slain by this one of hateful aspect — nor am I able to yield to his desire, as a twice-born man cannot impart a sacred mantra to one who is not twice-born."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ mamāṅgāny acirād anāryaḥ śastraiḥ śitaiś chetsyati rākṣasendraḥ tasminn anāgacchati lokanāthe garbhasthajantor iva śalyakṛntaḥ
english: "Surely this ignoble lord of rākṣasas will before long sever my limbs with sharp weapons — cutting like an arrow piercing a creature within the womb — since the lord of the worlds does not come."

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ batedaṃ mama duḥkhitāyā māsau cirāyābhigamiṣyato dvau baddhasya vadhyasya yathā niśānte rājāparādhād iva taskarasya
english: "How painful indeed are these two months that lie far ahead for me, afflicted as I am — like the night's end for a prisoner condemned to death, a thief who has offended the king."

sanskrit: hā rāma hā lakṣmaṇa hā sumitre hā rāma mātaḥ saha me jananyā eṣā vipadyāmy aham alpabhāgyā mahārṇave naur iva mūḍha vātā
english: "Alas Rāma! Alas Lakṣmaṇa! Alas Sumitrā! Alas Rāma, my mother and my birth-mother both — I, wretched and ill-fated, am perishing like a ship on the great ocean tossed by a wayward wind."

sanskrit: tarasvinau dhārayatā mṛgasya sattvena rūpaṃ manujendraputrau nūnaṃ viśastau mama kāraṇāt tau siṃharṣabhau dvāv iva vaidyutena
english: "Those two swift sons of the lord of men, those two lion-bulls, were surely slain on my account by that being that held the form of a deer — like two lightning-struck bulls."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ sa kālo mṛgarūpadhārī mām alpabhāgyāṃ lulubhe tadānīm yatrāryaputraṃ visasarja mūḍhā rāmānujaṃ lakṣmaṇapūrvakaṃ ca
english: "Surely that Time itself in the form of a deer lured me, wretched and ill-fated, at the moment when, deluded, I sent away my lord's son and also Rāma's younger brother, with Lakṣmaṇa going ahead."

sanskrit: hā rāma satyavrata dīrghavāho hā pūrṇacandrapratimānavaktra hā jīvalokasya hitaḥ priyaś ca vadhyāṃ na māṃ vetsi hi rākṣasānām
english: "Alas Rāma, keeper of vows and truth, O long-armed one! Alas, you whose face resembles the full moon! Alas, you who are the benefactor and beloved of all living beings — you do not know that I am being condemned to death by the rākṣasas!"

sanskrit: ananyadevatvam iyaṃ kṣamā ca bhūmau ca śayyā niyamaś ca dharme pativratātvaṃ viphalaṃ mamedaṃ kṛtaṃ kṛtaghneṣv iva mānuṣāṇām
english: "This devotion to none other than you, this forbearance, this sleeping on the ground, this adherence to dharma, this faithfulness as a wife — all this of mine has been done in vain, like kindness done to ungrateful men."

sanskrit: mogho hi dharmaś carito mamāyaṃ tathaikapatnītvam idaṃ nirartham yā tvāṃ na paśyāmi kṛśā vivarṇā hīnā tvayā saṃgamane nirāśā
english: "Indeed, the dharma I have practiced is in vain, and this fidelity to one husband is without purpose — I who am emaciated and pale do not see you, deprived of you, and without hope of union with you."

sanskrit: pitur nirdeśaṃ niyamena kṛtvā vanān nivṛttaś caritavrataś ca strībhis tu manye vipulekṣaṇābhiḥ saṃraṃsyase vītabhayaḥ kṛtārthaḥ
english: "Having dutifully fulfilled your father's command and having returned from the forest with your vow accomplished, I think you are now sporting with large-eyed women, free of fear, your purpose achieved."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu rāma tvayi jātakāmā ciraṃ vināśāya nibaddhabhāvā moghaṃ caritvātha tapovrataṃ ca tyakṣyāmi dhig jīvitam alpabhāgyā
english: "But I, Rāma, who conceived love for you, have long had my heart bound to destruction. Having practiced austerity and vows in vain, I, ill-fated, will abandon my life — fie upon this existence!"

sanskrit: sā jīvitaṃ kṣipram ahaṃ tyajeyaṃ viṣeṇa śastreṇa śitena vāpi viṣasya dātā na tu me 'sti kaś cic chastrasya vā veśmani rākṣasasya
english: "I would quickly abandon my life — by poison or by a sharp weapon — but there is none here in the rākṣasa's dwelling to give me poison or a weapon."

sanskrit: śokābhitaptā bahudhā vicintya sītātha veṇyudgrathanaṃ gṛhītvā udbadhya veṇyudgrathanena śīghram ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi yamasya mūlam
english: "Scorched by grief and having reflected in many ways, Sītā then resolved: taking the cord that binds my braid, I will quickly hang myself with it and go to Yama's abode."

sanskrit: itīva sītā bahudhā vilapya sarvātmanā rāmam anusmarantī pravepamānā pariśuṣkavaktrā nagottamaṃ puṣpitam āsasāda
english: Thus lamenting in many ways, with her whole being remembering Rāma, trembling, her face parched, Sītā approached a great flowering tree.

sanskrit: upasthitā sā mṛdur sarvagātrī śākhāṃ gṛhītvātha nagasya tasya tasyās tu rāmaṃ pravicintayantyā rāmānujaṃ svaṃ ca kulaṃ śubhāṅgyāḥ
english: She who was gentle in all her limbs drew near and grasped a branch of that tree. As she, of auspicious body, was deeply pondering upon Rāma, upon Rāma's younger brother, and upon her own lineage —

sanskrit: śokānimittāni tadā bahūni dhairyārjitāni pravarāṇi loke prādurnimittāni tadā babhūvuḥ purāpi siddhāny upalakṣitāni
english: — then many auspicious omens, foremost among those recognized in the world as causes of relief from sorrow, omens that had been proven true before as well, appeared to her.

sanskrit: tathāgatāṃ tāṃ vyathitām aninditāṃ vyapetaharṣāṃ paridīnamānasām śubhāṃ nimittāni śubhāni bhejire naraṃ śriyā juṣṭam ivopajīvinaḥ
english: As she stood thus — afflicted, blameless, drained of joy, her mind dejected, auspicious — auspicious omens befell her as dependants approach a man graced with fortune.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ śubhaṃ vāmam arālapakṣma rājīvṛtaṃ kṛṣṇaviśālaśuklam prāspandataikaṃ nayanaṃ sukeśyā mīnāhataṃ padmam ivābhitāmram
english: Her left eye — auspicious, with curved lashes, striped and reddened, with a large dark iris and white, that of the beautiful-haired one — began to quiver, like a lotus reddened by a fish striking it.

sanskrit: bhujaś ca cārvañcitapīnavṛttaḥ parārdhya kālāgurucandanārhaḥ anuttamenādhyuṣitaḥ priyeṇa cireṇa vāmaḥ samavepatāśu
english: And her left arm — gracefully curved, plump and rounded, worthy of priceless black aloe and sandalwood, long occupied by the most excellent beloved — quickly began to tremble.

sanskrit: gajendrahastapratimaś ca pīnas tayor dvayoḥ saṃhatayoḥ sujātaḥ praspandamānaḥ punar ūrur asyā rāmaṃ purastāt sthitam ācacakṣe
english: And her thigh — plump, resembling an elephant king's trunk, well-proportioned where the two thighs join — trembling again, seemed to point out Rāma standing before her.

sanskrit: śubhaṃ punar hemasamānavarṇam īṣadrajodhvastam ivāmalākṣyāḥ vāsaḥ sthitāyāḥ śikharāgradantyāḥ kiṃ cit parisraṃsata cārugātryāḥ
english: And the auspicious garment of the clear-eyed, beautiful-limbed one — golden in color, just slightly dulled with dust — slipped a little as she stood with teeth like the tips of lotus buds.

sanskrit: etair nimittair aparaiś ca subhrūḥ saṃbodhitā prāg api sādhusiddhaiḥ vātātapaklāntam iva pranaṣṭaṃ varṣeṇa bījaṃ pratisaṃjaharṣa
english: Awakened by these and other omens — proven true by the virtuous in earlier times as well — she of beautiful brows revived in joy, like a seed long wilted by wind and heat revived by rain.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ punar bimbaphalopamauṣṭhaṃ svakṣibhrukeśāntam arālapakṣma vaktraṃ babhāse sitaśukladaṃṣṭraṃ rāhor mukhāc candra iva pramuktaḥ
english: And her face once more shone forth — with lips like the bimba fruit, lovely eyes, brows and the hair's edge with curved lashes, with gleaming white teeth — like the moon released from Rāhu's mouth.

sanskrit: sā vītaśokā vyapanītatandrī śāntajvarā harṣavibuddhasattvā aśobhatāryā vadanena śukle śītānśunā rātrir ivoditena
english: She, freed of sorrow, her drowsiness dispelled, her fever calmed, her spirit awakened with joy, shone brilliantly with her noble face like a white night brightened by the risen cool-rayed moon.
